findings.description: The requirement detects a late-start fault when the task starts late but gives no detection deadline. CON-SUP-105 measures the safe-state reaction from expiry of the timing limit. OP-SYS-010 leaves detection for a task that never starts unresolved, so the required reaction cannot be verified for that case.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-010 as blocking and resolve when a late-start fault is detected, including when the task never starts.

findings.description: The requirement accepts a start at the limit and rejects a later start, but CON-SUP-103 specifies 100 µs measurement resolution. OP-SYS-009 leaves unresolved how starts in the measurement step containing the limit are classified, so the boundary result cannot be determined.
findings.requested_change: Classify OP-SYS-009 as blocking and decide the acceptance rule for starts in the measurement step containing the limit.

findings.description: Withholding every watchdog service immediately after detection can cause a window watchdog reset up to 12 ms after its previous refresh. A fault can occur just before that deadline, leaving insufficient time for the fault report and safe-state entry required before the supervisor reset by SYS-SUP-027 and CON-SUP-120.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the watchdog servicing and fault-recovery sequence so the report and safe-state entry can complete before a watchdog reset, with any necessary product decision recorded.

findings.description: The requirement reports a task name for every flow fault, but CON-SUP-104 includes missing and out-of-order checkpoints. An out-of-order sequence can involve more than one task, and no rule identifies which task name to report.
findings.requested_change: Define or obtain a decision on the entity reported for a flow fault when more than one task could be identified.
